answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit bond and files work in a shale ledger, each layer one task under one key. Each epoch a gale beacon draws 5% for audit, and the draw is public. An ocean panel of independent auditors replays the shale layers and burns the bond if a layer is copied, rented, or missing. The k-th fake needs its own 70-credit bond, so 1,000 fakes risk 70,000 credits, with 50 expected audits and a 3,500-credit burn every epoch. A rented layer fails because it carries its owner's signature, not the renter's. An honest agent posts once, pays one bond, and keeps it.
